content.title: Artemis II: Key moments in NASA’s historic moon mission
content.text: (FOX 5/KUSI) — The Artemis II astronauts have accomplished what no humans have done before them — became the first humans to travel the farthest distance into space and the first to see the dark side of the moon — during their historic lunar flyby mission. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency (CSA)’s Jeremy Hansen launched from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Wednesday, April 1. The crew’s mission was designed to put the Orion spacecraft through planned tests to see how well it performs in deep space. The astronauts also conducted lunar surface observations, human health studies and other critical activities throughout their 10-day mission. Artemis II builds on the success of NASA’s Artemis I mission in 2022, which was uncrewed. The Artemis II mission marks a milestone for NASA as the first mission with crew aboard the SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and Orion spacecraft. Want to relive key moments of the mission?
